nom: Drunk Elephant Scrubbi Bamboes Body Cleanser

segments.dry: One reviewer with typically drier skin reports her skin feels perfectly moisturized after use, and another notes the product leaves skin soft without irritation.
segments.sensitive: A reviewer who is sensitive to smell finds the scent light and tolerable, and another specifically sought a gentle wash without strong fragrance and found this suitable.

concerns.spots: One reviewer with generally normal skin reports the product made her skin breakout; no other reviewer reports new blemishes from use.
concerns.blemishes: Only one reviewer mentions breakouts as a result of using the product, while others describe skin as soft, smooth, or calm after use.
concerns.dehydration: Several reviewers describe skin as soft, smooth, or moisturized after use, including one who calls her skin typically on the drier side and found it well hydrated afterward.

aspects.libelle: Requires removing the cap to use
Scent described as absent or off

extraits.texte: I typically do not leave reviews, because everyone is different. Something I love another may hate. But, this product was so bad I needed to leave a review. For starters it smells like nothing, it's supposed to smell like vanilla.....that is untrue. Second, it is so thick it is impossible to squeeze out of the tiny hole. I had to take the cap off completely to even get any out. Third, it made my skin breakout. Fourth, the cost. The only upside to this product is that it does lather well and it did make my skin soft. But, with all the downsides, those two upsides are not worth it at all. I suggest you buy something else. Yes, Drunk Elephant is a great brand and has great products. However this is not one of them.

I typically prefer bar cleansers and wasn't a HUGE fan of the Kamili Body Cleanser, but I was intrigued by this product b/c I spend a lot of time outside and always feel a little grimy. I can't believe how much I love this cleanser! the faint vanilla smell is heavenly and the little scrubs perfectly buff away all the dirt and grime. My skin (which is typically on the drier side) always feels perfectly moisturized after using this. My ONLY complaint is the packaging. Although cute, it's not the greatest option to dispense this type of product. Hopefully it'll be released as a big version at some point!

I've tried so many body cleansers and body scrubs and this is like a 2 in 1. It's got just the right amount of exfoliation, not harsh but you can feel the little scrubby beads. I'm sensitive to smell but this has a light, not sweet vanilla-y scent. I wish they sold it in a bigger size tho because I run out fairly frequently. Love it!

I was looking for a gentle body wash that didn't have a sickeningly strong fragrance and this is it. It's just the right amount of exfoliation, not harsh and there's a very light vanilla-y scent. Wish the bottle was larger bc this is my 3rd purchase. Recommend!

I don't understand the negative reviews for this product. It has a lovely light natural scent, cleanses without irritating, and leaves my skin feeling smooth. I use it every other day. I have no problems getting it out of the bottle. A little bit goes a long way!

So i purchased this since theres a huge hype for Drunk Elephant. The product is too thick it wont come out of the bottle spout. Have to unscrew the cap to get product. The smell is horrible! It smells like its old or expired. Does not have a nice scent. Will be returning this!

The product itself is good. I would buy it again due to the natural ingredients, subtle scent and feel on my skin. THE REASON I WONT buy this again, though is so stupid. the packaging is awful. I cannot get the product out! It wasn't until almost my entire bottle was gone I realized I can add water into the wash to get it out, and then it all came out at once... just sad. Please fix packaging. I would buy if it were not for this. Every time I took a shower I literally thought omg. This is so frustrating I want to write a bad review. and here I am.

reserve: Most reviews focus on bottle design and scent rather than detailed skin-type or concern outcomes, so segment and concern coverage is thin and skewed toward packaging complaints.
